sentiment.instructions: These are Albanian (Kosovo Gheg dialect) Facebook comments on COVID-19 updates from Kosovo's public health institute (IKSHP). Judge the overall sentiment the commenter expresses toward the situation, the institutions or the news.

criteria.positive: Hope, relief, gratitude, praise, prayers or good wishes. Examples: falling case numbers celebrated, thanks to health staff, get-well wishes, encouragement to wear masks or follow measures. Cues: faleminderit/flm (thank you), respekt (respect), ju lumt (well done), sherim te shpejt (quick recovery), ishalla/inshalla (God willing), shpresojme (we hope), urime (congratulations), bravo, ma pak (fewer), po zbret (it's going down), mashalla, hajt se bahet mire (it'll be fine). Mild phrases such as 'not bad' also count as positive.
criteria.neutral: Bare tags of people's names, questions, factual statistics, jokes or banter without clear emotion, and neutral suggestions or speculation, e.g. asking which municipality, requesting more testing, or mixed remarks like 'good that numbers fell but bad that cases are new'. Calm advice or criticism without anger, insults or accusations of lying stays neutral.
criteria.negative: Anger, distrust, fear, mockery or despair. Examples: claiming the virus or numbers are lies, accusing institutions of failure or manipulation, insults, complaints about testing delays, alarm at rising cases, calls for blame. Cues: rrena/rrejt (lies), ska virus (there's no virus), turp (shame), marre (disgrace), keq (bad), tmerr (horror), deshtim (failure), na moren nqaf (they'll ruin us), skeni kontroll (you have no control), dallavere (scam).
